newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stock sentiment seen torn.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stock sentiment seen torn.

text.p: The Tokyo market's key index should be trapped in a narrow range this week, caught between two forces -- buying of financially healthy blue-chip issues, especially high techs, and the sell-off of shares in firms with financial problems, brokers said.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished at 19,875.49, down 92.51 points from the close a week earlier.

Market strategists expect the Nikkei 225 index to trade narrowly for the time being, as growing concerns about some Japanese companies, including contractors, retailers and brokers, weighed on the market.
But at the same time, such movements would prompt investors to actively seek promising issues.

"I expect the polarisation trend to continue next week, as high-techs will remain upbeat but issues with credit risks will decline," said Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

On Friday, Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher. "Worries over financially weak companies forced investors to hunt for issues backed by healthy earnings," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
The recent buying of high-technology issues was spurred by a winning streak of the Nasdaq composite index on Wall Street, brokers said.
Chris Calderwood, chief strategist at BZW Securities (Japan) Ltd said in a report issued last week that the rise in the Nikkei 225 would be weakened in the short term.

"Over the next few weeks we will probably see the market slip towards and below the 19,500 level on the Nikkei 225, but, if this does occur, we would view it as a selective buying opportunity," he said.
Some brokers said the Nikkei 225 index would not slide sharply unless some unexpected bankruptcy news came up.
"Unless there are surprise bankruptcies, the Nikkei 225 would not sink to 19,000," Karikomi said.
Brokers said the worries of some Japanese firms were triggered by the news earlier this month that a medium-sized contractor had filed for court protection from creditors.
On Friday, the top percentage losers were dominated by companies that have been dragged down by financial woes.
Shares of the supermarket chain operator Yaohan Japan Corp plunged by their daily limit to 93 yen, an all-time low. They closed at 95 yen, down 48 yen, or 33.57 percent.
Medium-sized contractor Tada Corp lost 50 yen, or 30.30 percent, to end at 115 yen.
Aoki Corp, another general contractor, was the third largest percentage loser, closing down 16 yen or 16 percent at 84 yen.
Shares of Sanyo Securities Co Ltd dropped 31 yen to close at 163.
Despite the gloom generated by certain issues, buying continued in high-tech issues.
Shares of Fujitsu Ltd, a major computer maker, rose 20 yen to 1,630. Advantest Corp, a measuring equipment and semiconductor maker, rose 610 yen to 9,650.
